1.w: The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord like channels of water; he turns it wherever he wants.

2.w: All a person’s ways seem right in his own opinion, but the Lord evaluates his thoughts.

3.w: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.

4.w: Haughty eyes and a proud heart— what the wicked cultivate is sin.

5.w: The plans of the diligent lead only to plenty, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty.

6.w: Making a fortune by a lying tongue is like a vapor driven back and forth; they seek death.

7.w: The violence done by the wicked will drag them away because they have refused to do what is right.

8.w: The way of the guilty person is devious, but as for the pure, his way is upright.

9.w: It is better to live on a corner of the housetop than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.

10.w: The appetite of the wicked has desired evil; his neighbor is shown no favor in his eyes.

11.w: When a scorner is punished, the naive becomes wise; when a wise person is instructed, he gains knowledge.

12.w: The Righteous One considers the house of the wicked; he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.

13.w: The one who shuts his ears to the cry of the poor, he too will cry out and will not be answered.

14.w: A gift given in secret subdues anger, and a bribe given secretly subdues strong wrath.

15.w: Doing justice brings joy to the righteous and terror to those who do evil.

16.w: The one who wanders from the way of wisdom will end up in the company of the departed.

17.w: The one who loves pleasure will be a poor person; whoever loves wine and anointing oil will not be rich.

18.w: The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous are taken in the place of the upright.

19.w: It is better to live in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome and easily provoked woman.

20.w: There is desirable treasure and olive oil in the dwelling of the wise, but a foolish person devours all he has.

21.w: The one who pursues righteousness and love finds life, bounty, and honor.

22.w: A wise man went up against the city of the mighty and brought down the stronghold in which they trust.

23.w: The one who guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his life from troubles.

24.w: A proud and arrogant person, whose name is “Scoffer,” acts with overbearing pride.

25.w: What the sluggard desires will kill him, for his hands have refused to work.

26.w: All day long he has craved greedily, but the righteous person gives and does not hold back.

27.w: The wicked person’s sacrifice is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with evil intent!

28.w: A lying witness will perish, but the one who reports accurately speaks forever.

29.w: A wicked person has put on a bold face, but as for the upright, he establishes his ways.

30.w: There is no wisdom and there is no understanding, and there is no counsel against the Lord .

31.w: A horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the victory is from the Lord .
